recapTopic: AI Visibility and Search Optimization for B2B

recap.intro: Hey everyone! This week, we dove into how AI, like ChatGPT and Google's AI answers, is changing how businesses get found online.
bullets: First, we saw that even though everyone's talking about AI, tools like ChatGPT actually send super little traffic to websites – like, only 0.62% of what regular Google search does. While those few AI visitors might be really interested and buy stuff (one study showed they converted 4.5 times better!), Google still brings in way more total sales. So, think of showing up in AI as more like a 'digital billboard' for your brand, building awareness rather than getting direct clicks.

Building on that, we learned why it's still super important to show up in AI. People are now asking AI tools for recommendations *before* they even visit a website, and when Google shows an AI summary (that quick answer generated by AI), people often stop looking further! This is a big deal, especially since 18% of Google searches in March 2025 had these AI summaries. That's why tools like Scrunch are popping up, which can even show a special, simplified version of your website just for AI bots, while Ahrefs Brand Radar helps you track where your brand is mentioned by AI across places like YouTube and TikTok.

Finally, we tied it all together by looking at the real-world challenges. Even though most marketing teams (86.4%!) are using AI, a huge chunk (33%) struggle to prove if all that automated effort actually makes more money. We found out it's usually not the tool's fault; the real problems are things like not having a clear plan, using bad customer information (which makes automation send wrong messages super fast!), or different tools not talking to each other. So, having a solid strategy and good data is key for AI to actually help your business grow.

headline: Digital marketing strategy for B2B business: the parts, and why they have to work together
keyNotes: For businesses that sell to other businesses (what we call B2B), having a well-thought-out plan for how they do their online marketing is essential.
The article highlights that for this online marketing plan to truly work, all its different pieces, or "components," must be connected and work together.
This idea of making sure everything is connected and working as one unit is called building a "cohesive" strategy, and it's presented as a key to success.
Ultimately, the main goal of having all these online marketing parts work together is to help the business achieve success that lasts for a long time.
question: The article emphasizes that for a business's online marketing to succeed long-term, all its parts must work together. In your own work, what are the different 'parts' or tasks you handle, and how well do they currently connect and support each other to achieve your long-term goals?
